README: The sound sheet. Three years of the same night, so the music barely moves: one low note under the hook, a slower one under the grind, and it only opens up when the player list changes. Silence is used once — on 'It's still here. I kept it.' — because that is the line the whole film is written to reach. Every effect mirrors something on screen: a coin, a torch, a block set down, one name appearing on a list.

A sign put up just in case, for somebody who may never read it.
Silence for the line the film was written to reach: 'It's still here. I kept it.'
Friday. One player. The same low note as the opening, because nothing has changed yet.
The list moves. One becomes two.
His name, after three years: the film's one arrival, and it is seven letters of pixel text.
He sits without moving for an hour, so the music does not move either.
He walks the whole castle without saying a word. The boy has been waiting three years for this.
He puts down the last block himself.
'I watched the map. Every Sunday.' Three years of nights, answered in six words.
The castle is finished, by both of them, in the first light of a Friday morning.
